title: Stop retrying a job forever

blocks.text: The job runner takes jobs from a broker. When a delivery fails, the runner asks `RetryPolicy` whether to put the job back, and a job that keeps failing is meant to be dropped after a few deliveries. Each delivery is read from its message into a new `Job` object. `Job` is a record that the producer shares, and the first attempt to count deliveries in a field of `Job` didn't compile.

Finish `failed(...)` and `failures(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/RetryPolicy.java`. A job is delivered at most `maxDeliveries` times, and its count must not depend on which `Job` object a delivery arrived in. You may add fields to `RetryPolicy`, but don't change `Job`. About four lines in total.

cases.says: a job is delivered again after each failure until it has failed the maximum number of times
the failures of one job don't count against another job
a job that arrives again as a new but equal object keeps the failures of its earlier deliveries

origin.section: Keep a Class for Identity, Changing State, or Many Optional Parts

concepts: State that changes over a record's life, such as a retry count, lives outside the record, in a map keyed by it, not in a static field of the record.
A record's equals compares components, so two distinct things with the same data are one entry, and a new equal record is the same map key.
